data.value: Enable built-in 16:9 widescreen patches where available. Best applied before starting a game.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_no_interlacing_patches.Label
data.value: Apply game patches to disable interlacing

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_no_interlacing_patches.Help
data.value: Enable built-in progressive-output patches where available. Best applied before starting a game.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_mtvu.Label
data.value: Run VU1 on a separate thread (MTVU)

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_mtvu.Help
data.value: Runs VU1 on its own thread. Large speedup on multi-core CPUs; a small number of games hang with it.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_instant_vu1.Help
data.value: Runs VU1 to completion immediately (ignored while MTVU is enabled). Usually a speedup.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_ee_cycle_rate.Help
data.value: Set the emulated Emotion Engine clock relative to its normal speed. 100% is the original clock. Lower or higher clocks can help some games but may cause problems. This does not set the playback speed of the whole emulator.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_ee_cycle_skip.Help
data.value: Makes the EE skip cycles. Helps some games with high VU activity, breaks others.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_cpu_recompiler.Help
data.value: Uses dynamic recompilation for the EE, IOP and vector processors. This is faster than interpretation. Disable only to diagnose compatibility problems.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_rec_ee.Help
data.value: Diagnostic. Disable just the Emotion Engine (EE) dynarec while leaving the others on.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_rec_iop.Help
data.value: Diagnostic. Disable just the IOP (R3000) dynarec while leaving the others on.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_rec_vu0.Help
data.value: Diagnostic. Disable just the VU0 microVU dynarec while leaving the others on.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_rec_vu1.Help
data.value: Diagnostic. Disable just the VU1 microVU dynarec while leaving the others on.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_memcard_slot1_enable.Help
data.value: Enable the Slot 1 PS2 memory card. Changes apply immediately while content is running.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_memcard_slot2_enable.Help
data.value: Enable the Slot 2 PS2 memory card. Changes apply immediately while content is running.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_ppu_decoder.Help
data.value: Choose how to execute instructions for the PPU, which is the main CPU. Recompilation with LLVM is the fastest method.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_spu_decoder.Help
data.value: Choose how to execute instructions for the SPU coprocessors. Recompilation with LLVM is the fastest method.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_spu_block_size.Help
data.value: SPU recompiler block size. Mega/Giga may improve performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_accurate_rsx_reservation.Help
data.value: Synchronize RSX memory accesses with the reservations of the CPU threads. Needed by a few games, slower.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_spu_accurate_dma.Help
data.value: Accurately processes SPU DMA operations, as in RPCS3. Fixes a few games, at a large cost in speed.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_spu_accurate_reservations.Help
data.value: Accurately processes SPU reservations, as in RPCS3 (on by default there too). Turning it off can make some games faster and break others.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_debug_console_mode.Help
data.value: Emulates a PS3 debug console (more memory and debug features) instead of a retail one. Only for software that needs it; not recommended otherwise.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_mfc_delay_command.Help
data.value: Delays every second MFC (SPU DMA) command, as in RPCS3. Only for the few games that need it.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_disable_getllar_spin_opt.Help
data.value: Turn off the detection of SPU busy-wait loops on GETLLAR. A few games need it off.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_emulate_hdd_speed.Help
data.value: Reads from the emulated hard disk at the speed of the PS3's, for games that break when loading is instant.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_emulate_bdvd_speed.Help
data.value: Reads from the disc at the PS3 drive's 2x speed (9 MB/s), for games that stream movies from disc and show corrupted video when loading is instant. Loading takes longer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_ppu_reservation_priority.Help
data.value: Gives PPU reservations priority over the SPUs', as in RPCS3. Can help games that stall on them.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_llvm_precompilation.Help
data.value: Precompile PPU modules at boot for faster subsequent loads.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_frame_limit.Help
data.value: Highest frame rate the game may run at. Auto is the VBlank Frequency, as in RPCS3; PS3 Native paces flips the way the PS3 does; Off lets games that do not wait for the PS3's refresh themselves run too fast.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_msaa.Help
data.value: Multi-sample anti-aliasing where the game asks for it, as in RPCS3.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_zcull_accuracy.Help
data.value: How exactly occlusion queries are answered, as in RPCS3. Precise is correct and the default there; Approximate and Relaxed are faster, and can break effects such as lens flares. Relaxed is worth trying on phones.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_shader_quality.Help
data.value: Precision of the shaders RPCS3 generates. Low is fastest, Ultra most accurate.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_default_resolution.Help
data.value: The output resolution the emulated PS3 offers the game, as in RPCS3. Most games run at 720p; some look better at 1080p, and some need 480p or 576p to avoid bugs. Takes effect when content is loaded.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_resolution_scale.Help
data.value: Internal rendering resolution as a percentage of the game's own. 200% of a 720p game is 2560x1440, of a 1080p one 3840x2160.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_scale_threshold.Help
data.value: Render targets smaller than this are not scaled. Some games need a different value for the scaling to look right.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_shader_mode.Help
data.value: How shaders are compiled. Async compiles in the background but the frame that first needs a pipeline waits for it, which is what a long freeze on a new scene usually is. Async with Shader Interpreter draws that frame through the interpreter instead and swaps in the compiled shader when it is ready: no freeze, lower speed while it catches up.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_write_color_buffers.Help
data.value: Write color buffers to main memory. Fixes some effects.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_stretch_to_display.Help
data.value: Stretch game output to fill the display, reported to RetroArch at this aspect ratio: pick the display's for games patched to a wider one (21:9, 32:9). Needs RetroArch's aspect ratio set to Core Provided.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_multithreaded_rsx.Help
data.value: Moves part of the RSX work to a second thread. Off by default, as in RPCS3; it can help on CPUs with few fast cores, phones included.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_host_gpu_labels.Help
data.value: Lets the host GPU signal RSX labels itself instead of the CPU waiting on them. Faster in some games, unstable in others.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_disable_blit_upscaling.Label
data.value: Do not increase resolution for image copies made by the graphics processor

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_disable_blit_upscaling.Help
data.value: Keep image copies made by the RSX graphics engine at the original game resolution, as in RPCS3. Do not apply the selected resolution scale to these copies. This fixes effects in some games when using higher resolutions, but these parts of the image may look less sharp.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_disable_vertex_cache.Help
data.value: Turn off the cache of vertex data, as in RPCS3. Slower; only for games that show broken or stale geometry with it.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_emulate_depth_compare.Help
data.value: Emulates the depth comparison modes the PS3 has and the host GPU lacks. Fixes some shadows, at a cost in speed.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_force_hw_msaa_resolve.Help
data.value: Resolves anti-aliased surfaces on the GPU's own hardware instead of a shader. Faster, but some games show artifacts with it.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_handle_tiled_memory.Help
data.value: Emulates the RSX's tiled memory, for games that read their tiled surfaces back. Costs speed.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_read_depth_buffers.Help
data.value: Read depth buffers from main memory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_read_color_buffers.Help
data.value: Read color buffers from main memory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_use_rebar.Label
data.value: Use Re-BAR Memory for GPU Uploads

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_use_rebar.Help
data.value: Uploads to the GPU through resizable BAR memory where the Vulkan driver offers it, as in RPCS3 (on by default there too). Turn off if it causes problems.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_write_depth_buffers.Help
data.value: Write depth buffers to main memory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_driver_wakeup_delay.Help
data.value: Driver wake-up delay in microseconds. 0 by default, as in RPCS3; raise it only when a game needs it.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_vblank_rate.Help
data.value: Sets the emulated refresh rate. The compatibility-list mode doubles it for supported games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_thread_scheduler.Help
data.value: Who places the emulator's threads on the CPU's cores, as in RPCS3. Operating System leaves it to the system; the RPCS3 schedulers pin PPU, SPU and RSX threads to cores of their own, laid out for a few desktop CPUs. Has no effect on Android, where the core cannot pin threads.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_preferred_spu_threads.Help
data.value: Number of SPU threads. Auto recommended.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_spu_loop_detection.Help
data.value: Detects SPU loops that only wait and skips through them. Faster, but some games break with it; off by default, as in RPCS3. Worth turning on for speed on phones.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_llvm_threads.Help
data.value: Choose how many threads compile PPU and SPU code with LLVM. This corresponds to the compilation thread limit in RPCS3. Automatic mode uses all processor cores, except efficiency cores on ARM processors that have them, such as most phones and some laptops. Fewer threads reduce heat and memory use during compilation, but make compilation slower.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_shader_compiler_threads.Label
data.value: Number of threads used to compile shaders

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_shader_compiler_threads.Help
data.value: How many threads compile shaders. Auto lets RPCS3 decide from the CPU it sees. On ARM CPUs with efficiency cores (most phones, some ARM laptops) the default leaves those out.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_ppu_threads.Help
data.value: How many PPU threads run at once, as in RPCS3. 2 is the default and what nearly every game wants.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_max_spurs_threads.Help
data.value: Maximum SPURS thread count. Lower may improve performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_max_preempt_count.Help
data.value: How many times a frame RPCS3 may pause the CPU threads to save power, as in RPCS3. 0 turns it off.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_network_enabled.Help
data.value: Lets games reach the internet. Takes effect when content is loaded.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_psn_status.Help
data.value: What games see of the PlayStation Network. Simulated makes them believe they are signed in, which some need to get past their menus; RPCN connects to RPCS3's own server and needs Network Enabled and an RPCN account: the core cannot create one, so set it up in standalone RPCS3 and copy its rpcn.yml into system/rpcs3/ (system/rpcs3/config/ on Windows). Takes effect when content is loaded.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_upnp.Help
data.value: Enable UPnP for automatic port forwarding.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_disable_fifo_reordering.Help
data.value: Turns off the reordering of RSX commands RPCS3 does for speed. For debugging.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_disable_hw_blending.Help
data.value: Forces programmable blending on renderers that support it, as in RPCS3's Debug tab. Purely a debugging option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_disable_hw_colorspace.Label
data.value: Disable color space conversion in the graphics hardware

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_disable_hw_colorspace.Help
data.value: Remaps texture colour spaces in shaders instead of in the GPU's hardware. For debugging.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_disable_zcull_queries.Help
data.value: Always report that objects are visible, without testing whether another object hides them. This improves speed, but can break games that use these tests for visibility or lens flare effects.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_cpu_blit.Help
data.value: Force CPU blit emulation for certain effects.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_gpu_texture_scaling.Help
data.value: Scales textures on the GPU instead of the CPU. For debugging; can break games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_spu_events_busy_loop.Help
data.value: Lets SPU threads spin while they wait for events instead of sleeping. Can help a few games, costs CPU time.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_set_daz_ftz.Help
data.value: Sets the denormals-are-zero and flush-to-zero CPU flags for the PPU. For debugging.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_accurate_ppu_128.Help
data.value: Processes 128-byte PPU reservation operations accurately: never, always, or for loops up to the given length. For debugging.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_fb_aliasing_bias.Help
data.value: Which way RPCS3 decides a surface used as both colour and depth. For debugging.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_database_override.Help
data.value: Improves compatibility by automatically applying game-specific fixes: the settings RPCS3's database has for the game (as standalone RPCS3 applies them) take priority over the core options, global or per game, for the settings they name; every other setting stays as you set it. Off applies none of them. Takes effect the next time a game is started.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_perf_overlay.Help
data.value: Display performance information from RPCS3 over the game image. This includes the frame rate measured by RPCS3. Higher detail levels also show the time taken by each frame and the CPU and GPU load.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_frame_pacing.Help
data.value: What the game's frames are timed by. Emulator clock is RPCS3's own timer, as in standalone RPCS3. RetroArch gives the game one PS3 refresh per frame RetroArch shows, so fast-forward speeds the game up and the game runs at the VBlank Frequency when RetroArch shows that many frames a second; with the Vulkan renderer it currently skips frames.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_show_ppu_compilation_hint.Help
data.value: Show hint when PPU modules are being compiled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_show_shader_compilation_hint.Label
data.value: Show a message while shaders are being compiled

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_show_shader_compilation_hint.Help
data.value: Show hint when shaders are being compiled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_silence_all_logs.Help
data.value: Silence all log output for performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_spu_cache.Help
data.value: Enable SPU cache for faster subsequent loads.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_accurate_dfma.Help
data.value: Double-precision fused multiply-add done exactly, as in RPCS3 (on by default there too). Costs little on CPUs with FMA; turning it off can help on a slow phone, and breaks some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_driver_recovery_timeout.Help
data.value: GPU driver recovery timeout in milliseconds.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_vblank_ntsc.Help
data.value: Run the VBlank Frequency at the NTSC rate (59.94 Hz for 60) instead of the round number. On by default, as in RPCS3.

data.name: Emulation.Option.play.Resolution.Help
data.value: Selects the internal rendering resolution multiplier.

data.name: Emulation.Option.play.Presentation.Help
data.value: Fits the image, fills the screen or preserves the original size.

data.name: Emulation.Option.play.Bilinear.Help
data.value: Forces bilinear texture filtering in the renderer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Controller.AnalogDirections
data.value: Use analog sticks for digital directions

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Controller.AnalogCalibration.Short
data.value: Scales the measured analog axis range for games that expect larger input values. Move the axes through their full range after loading a game.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.Fastboot.Help
data.value: Skips BIOS startup screen and boots straight to the game. Disable this if you want to access the PS2 system settings or access the Memory Card manager.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.Fastcdvd.Help
data.value: Fast CD/DVD access/seek times. A small handful of games will have compatibility problems with this enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.SharedMemoryCards.Help
data.value: Use per-content or shared memory cards.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.EnableCheats.Help
data.value: Read game cheat codes from files in the selected folder.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.HintLanguageUnlock.Help
data.value: If enabled, will look inside the internal database for language unlock options. Examples include: forcing an international Japanese version to English, unlocking more European languages, etc

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.Dev9Hdd.Help
data.value: Emulate the SPEED expansion's ATA hard drive. The image lives at 'pcsx2/DEV9hdd.raw' in the frontend system directory and is created on first use at the configured size.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.Dev9HddSize.Help
data.value: Capacity used when a new HDD image is created. An existing image keeps the size it was created with.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.Dev9Eth.Help
data.value: Emulate the SPEED expansion's ethernet adapter through the Sockets backend: a userspace TCP/UDP stack with an internal DHCP server, needing no host network configuration or privileges.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.UpscaleMultiplier.Help
data.value: Draw at a multiple of the PS2's resolution. The software renderers draw at 2x for 2x and above.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.NativeScaling.Label
data.value: Keep effects at the console's original resolution

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.NativeScaling.Help
data.value: Render the buffers a game draws at a fraction of its frame, such as a bloom or blur pass, at native resolution instead of the internal resolution. Keeps a blur's radius and position as on the console, at the cost of the resolution of the blurred picture; 'Aggressive' also applies to the draws that scale those buffers back up. 'Automatic' uses the game database's setting for the game, or 'Normal' where it has none. Any other value is used regardless of the database and of 'Enable HW Hacks'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.PgsSsaa.Help
data.value: Apply supersampled anti-aliasing (SSAA). Unlike straight upscaling, supersampling retains a coherent visual look where 3D elements have similar resolution as UI elements. For 2x high-res scanout you need at least '4x SSAA ordered' (or higher); 4x high-res scanout needs '16x SSAA (ordered)' specifically -- the plain 16x mode uses a sparse grid that only supports 2x. '32x SSAA (ordered)' is a 4x8 grid, four samples across and eight down: it also feeds the 4x scanout at the full field height, which gives field-rendered games twice the vertical resolution of 16x ordered, at twice its cost. Setting this to 'Native' disables super sampling.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.PgsHighResScanout.Help
data.value: Scans out above native resolution with paraLLEl (2x: 640x448 becomes 1280x896; 4x: 2560x1792). Doesn't work with every game, some might require patches on top. 2x requires Supersampling at 4x SSAA ordered or higher; 4x requires 16x SSAA ordered, and falls back to 2x on lower grids. At 16x SSAA with plain 4x scanout the whole sample grid is spent on resolution, so edges keep no residual anti-aliasing; the anti-aliased 4x mode instead reconstructs each output pixel from the neighboring samples with a tent filter, trading a slight softness for far less texture shimmer. A game that renders one field at a time gets half the height from 4x (2560x896); the full field height mode gives it the whole 2560x1792 and needs 32x SSAA ordered, falling back to the plain 4x on smaller grids. Its anti-aliased variant applies the same tent reconstruction at that height, and falls back to the anti-aliased 4x on smaller grids.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.PgsSsTex.Help
data.value: Feedback higher resolution textures. With super sampling on, a copy of the picture (a post-processing pass that moves it texel for pixel) always keeps its super samples; enabling this also feeds them to blurs and other effects that read the picture back. May help high-res scanout image quality. Highly experimental and may cause rendering glitches.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.PgsDeblur.Help
data.value: Attempts to workaround games that add extra blit passes before scanning out. May lead to better image quality in certain games which do this.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.PgsDisableMipmaps.Help
data.value: Disable this for traditional hardware mipmapping. Enabling this will bypass mipmapping and always use texture LOD0 instead. The result is better image quality. Only a small handful of games have graphics rendering issues with this enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.DeinterlaceMode.Help
data.value: Select a deinterlacing method. Use 'Automatic' if unsure what to pick.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.HwDownloadMode.Help
data.value: Controls how the GS reads rendered data back to the CPU (e.g. memory-card save images). 'Accurate' is the safest and matches hardware, but forces a CPU/GPU synchronization on every readback, which can sharply reduce the frame rate on screens that read back often (some save/load and stage-select menus) - this is especially severe with the paraLLEl-GS renderer. 'Unsynchronized' avoids that stall and is much faster, at the risk of incorrect results in the rare games that read back GPU-rendered content. 'Disable Readbacks' and 'Disabled' trade more accuracy for speed.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.NointerlacingHint.Help
data.value: If enabled, will look in the internal database if a patch is available for the game to turn the image into either a non-interlaced, full frame, or progressive scan video signal, and/or a combination of all the above. Image will be more stable and Deinterlacing can be turned off.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.WidescreenHint.Help
data.value: Applies a widescreen patch if a patch for the game can be found inside the internal database.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.PcrtcAntiblur.Help
data.value: Disable this for the most accurate output image. Enabling this will attempt to deblur the image. Most noticeable on software renderer and paraLLEl.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.DisableInterlaceOffset.Label
data.value: Disable the vertical offset used for interlaced video

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.SwRendererThreads.Label
data.value: CPU threads used for software rendering

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.SwRendererThreads.Help
data.value: Number of extra worker threads the software renderer rasterizes with, on top of the GS thread itself. 0 rasterizes on the GS thread alone (lowest latency, best on 2-4 core CPUs). More threads help scenes with many alpha effects on CPUs with spare cores. Only used by the software renderer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.VuAccurateAddsub.Help
data.value: Model the VU adder's exponent-distance truncation on every add and subtract. The Tri-Ace games that require this behaviour (Star Ocean 3, Radiata Stories, Valkyrie Profile 2) get it automatically per title via the game database even when this is disabled; enable it globally only when chasing accuracy in other titles. Costs speed on VU-heavy games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.EeAccurateFpu.Help
data.value: Run EE FPU add, sub, mul and the fused chains through the extended-range double pipeline: exact add/sub against the hardware model, near-exact multiplies, correct handling of the huge values the PS2 allows, exact integer conversion, and pure-bitop ABS/NEG. Measured free at workload level (within run noise on frame throughput); enabled by default.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.VuExactMul.Help
data.value: Bit-exact hardware model of the VU multiplier. Real game data trips the full model on most multiplies - zeros, ones and quantized values dominate - so expect a real speed cost on VU-heavy games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.VuExactDiv.Help
data.value: Bit-exact hardware model of the VU divider (DIV, SQRT, RSQRT).

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.FpuSoftfloat.Help
data.value: Route recompiled EE FPU arithmetic through the bit-exact software FPU. Interpreted FPU code is always bit-exact; this extends it to the recompiler at some speed cost. Fixes games whose logic depends on exact console FPU results.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.Vu0Softfloat.Help
data.value: Run VU0 micro programs on the bit-exact interpreter, whose float ops compute through the console-exact software model, instead of the SSE recompiler. Macro-mode COP2 code is not covered by this option. Costly; enable per game when exact VU0 results matter.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.Vu1Softfloat.Help
data.value: Run VU1 on the bit-exact interpreter, whose float ops compute through the console-exact software model, instead of the SSE recompiler. Fixes games whose rendering depends on exact console VU results. Significantly costly and scales with scene complexity; enable per game only when required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.EeCpu.Help
data.value: Selects what executes Emotion Engine code. Recompiler is the normal choice. Interpreter runs the EE in plain C: far too slow for play, but it takes the EE recompiler out of the picture entirely, so a hang that survives it is not a codegen bug. Selecting Interpreter also disables Fastmem, which only applies to the recompiler.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.Fastmem.Help
data.value: Backs guest memory accesses with a direct 4GB mapping and patches out the ones that fault. Disable to route every access through the software memory handlers - slower, but takes the fastmem fault/backpatch machinery out of the picture entirely, which is useful when hunting a hang.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.Mtvu.Help
data.value: Runs VU1 on its own thread. Large speedup on multi-core CPUs; a small number of games hang with it. The default matches the platform default (on arm64, MTVU is on whenever the native VU1 recompiler drives VU1).

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.GameEnhancementsHint.Help
data.value: Applies game-specific enhancements if patches for the game can be found inside the internal database. Examples of enhancements: LOD [Level of Detail] enhancements, better draw distance, ability to skip FMVs, etc.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.UncappedFramerateHint.Help
data.value: Uncaps the framerate if a patch for the game can be found inside the internal database. This can turn a 30fps game into 60fps locked, or stabilize the framerate. You might have to increase EE Cycle Rate in combination with this for a stable locked framerate. 60fps PAL-to-NTSC does what it says if it can find a patch, otherwise it will just try to use the default uncapped framerate patch (50fps for PAL, 60fps for NTSC)

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.EnableHwHacks.Help
data.value: This will disable automatic settings from the database. Unless you know what you are doing it is NOT RECOMMENDED to turn this ON.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.CpuSpriteSize.Label
data.value: Maximum width of 2D SPRITES rendered by CPU

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.UseExternalGameindex.Help
data.value: Requires a hardware renderer and manual rendering fixes. Load the selected game compatibility database.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.UnscaledPaletteDraw.Label
data.value: Draw palette textures at the original resolution

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.InvertLeftStick.Label
data.value: Invert the axes of the left analog stick

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.InvertRightStick.Label
data.value: Invert the axes of the right analog stick

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.AnalogMode.Help
data.value: Start the controller in analog mode rather than digital. Some games (e.g. Ridge Racer V) boot the pad in digital and normally require pressing the controller's ANALOG button to enable the sticks; enable this to get analog controls from the start. Games that lock the controller mode are unaffected.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.ForceAnalog.Help
data.value: Forces analog mode to be always on. May cause issues with some games. Only use this option for games that support analog mode but do not automatically enable it themselves. When disabled, analog mode can be toggled by pressing and holding the DualShock Analog Mode Combo.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.AnalogToggle.Help
data.value: When the input device type is DualShock, this option allows the emulated DualShock to be toggled between DIGITAL and ANALOG mode like original hardware. Mode can also be toggled by using the selected button combination.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.AnalogToggleCombo.Help
data.value: The button combination that will be used to toggle between DIGITAL and ANALOG mode for the emulated DualShock.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.AnalogToggleHold.Label
data.value: DualShock Analog Mode Combo Hold Delay

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.AnalogToggleHold.Help
data.value: Hold time for the analog mode combo buttons.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.NegconDeadzone.Help
data.value: Left analog stick deadzone when simulating the 'twist' action of emulated 'neGcon' input devices. Used to eliminate controller drift. Note: Most neGcon-compatible titles provide in-game options for setting a 'twist' deadzone value. To avoid loss of precision, the in-game deadzone should *always* be set to zero. Any required adjustments should *only* be applied via this core option. This is particularly important when 'neGcon Twist Response' is set to 'Quadratic' or 'Cubic'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.SecondMemoryCard.Help
data.value: Emulate a second memory card in the right memory card slot. Note: Some games require this option to be disabled for correct operation (e.g. Codename Tenka). Note: Memory Card Slot 2 uses the Mednafen (.mcr) save format.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.SharedMemoryCardMethod.Help
data.value: Use shared memory cards instead of separate cards for each content. Note: if 'Memory Card Method' is set to 'Libretro', only memory card slot 2 will be affected.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.LineToQuad.Help
data.value: Some games (e.g. Doom, Hexen, Soul Blade, etc.) draw horizontal lines by stretching single-pixel-high triangles across the screen, which are rasterized as a row of pixels on original hardware. This hack detects these small triangles and converts them to quads as required, allowing them to be displayed properly on the hardware renderers and at upscaled internal resolutions. 'Aggressive' is required for some titles (e.g. Dark Forces, Duke Nukem) but may otherwise introduce graphical glitches. Leave at 'Default' if unsure.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Setting.DynarecEventCycles.Help
data.value: Max cycles run by CPU before a GPU/DMA/MDEC/Timer Update is checked, higher number will be faster, has much less impact on beetle interpreter than dynarec.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_aspect_ratio.Help
data.value: Sets the screen format reported to games. Only some games support 4:3.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_disk_cache_size.Help
data.value: Limits disk space used for temporary game caches. Games rebuild deleted caches, which can slow the next start.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokket.Help
data.value: Insert a card in each unit to enable the infrared link.

data.name: Emulation.Option.rpcs3.rpcs3_audio_format.Help
data.value: Sets the speaker layout offered to games. The game selects its audio mix from this layout. Output also depends on the selected Windows audio device.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcee2.pcsx2_cheats.Help
data.value: Loads .pnach cheat files from the selected folder. Use filenames containing the game serial number and CRC. Files are read when a game starts.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_dynarec_eventcycles.Help
data.value: Checks DMA, graphics, video decoding and timer events after at most this many CPU cycles. Values increase by 128. Higher values can improve performance but reduce timing accuracy.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_dynarec_eventcycles.Help
data.value: Checks DMA, graphics, video decoding and timer events after at most this many CPU cycles. Values increase by 128. Higher values can improve performance but reduce timing accuracy.

data.name: Emulation.Sony.Ethernet.Help
data.value: Uses the emulator's socket network backend with automatic host interface selection and DHCP handling. Configure the network connection inside the PS2 game. Changing this setting requires restarting the machine.
